title: Freshservice Microsoft Teams Integration in 2026
summary: Explore Freshservice Microsoft Teams integration in 2026 for ticket management, notifications, and IT support.
body_markdown:
Every IT team knows the drill: someone pings a Slack channel about a broken laptop, another employee DMs HR about parental leave, and a third sends an email asking for procurement approval on new software licenses. Without a structured internal help desk, requests can become scattered across conversations, inboxes, and portals.


Freshservice offers a Microsoft Teams integration designed to bring service desk workflows into Teams. Through ServiceBot, IT and internal operations teams can receive ticket notifications, approve requests, and take ticket actions without constantly switching between Teams and Freshservice.


But there is a meaningful difference between extending a portal-based ITSM platform into Teams and using an internal help desk designed around conversational employee support. For organizations evaluating access management, laptop replacements, onboarding tasks, expense approvals, and other internal requests, that distinction matters.


This article explains how Freshservice's Teams integration works, where it fits, and when a chat-native approach to[internal help desk automation](https://unthread.io/solutions/it-service-desk/?ref=unthread.io) may better match employee workflows.


## **Key Takeaways**


- Freshservice uses ServiceBot to bring ticket notifications, approvals, and selected service desk actions into Microsoft Teams.
- Freshservice remains centered on its broader ITSM platform, with Teams acting as another interface for parts of the service workflow.
- Freshservice is well suited to organizations that need established ITSM capabilities such as ticketing, asset management, change management, and service catalogs.
- Unthread takes a different approach by turning conversations in Slack and Microsoft Teams into trackable internal requests.
- Unthread's purpose-built AI agent can automate workflows across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, Finance, and other internal teams. Lemonade reports approximately[40% automatic resolution](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across multiple departments.


## **Understanding Freshservice and Its Role in Internal Service Management**


Freshservice is a cloud-based IT service management platform from Freshworks. It supports ticketing, asset management, service catalogs, change management, and other structured ITSM workflows.


For internal teams, these capabilities can support requests such as software provisioning, hardware issues, onboarding, access changes, and approvals. Microsoft Teams extends parts of this service desk experience into the collaboration environment employees and agents already use.


The distinction is architectural. Freshservice remains the underlying service management platform, while Teams provides another interaction point for notifications, approvals, and service desk actions.


Organizations already using Freshservice can therefore add Teams to their existing processes without replacing the broader ITSM environment.


## **Freshservice Microsoft Teams Integration: Core Features and Setup**


The Freshservice Microsoft Teams integration centers on ServiceBot, which connects service desk activity with Teams.


### **What ServiceBot Does**


ServiceBot can support several internal service workflows inside Teams:


- **Ticket notifications:** Agents can receive updates related to service desk activity.
- **Interactive actions:** Teams notifications can provide actions associated with requests.
- **Collaboration:** Teams can support conversations around service requests and internal workflows.
- **Approval workflows:** Managers and other stakeholders can respond to approval requests from Teams.


These capabilities can be useful for IT, HR, Finance, Procurement, and other internal teams that want service desk activity to appear closer to their everyday collaboration workflows.


### **Setup Process**


Freshservice administrators configure the Microsoft Teams connection from Freshservice and authorize the integration with Microsoft 365.


The exact configuration depends on which Freshservice capabilities an organization wants to expose through Teams. Teams administrators and service desk administrators may also need to coordinate permissions, users, and notification settings.


For organizations already operating Freshservice, this model can extend existing service processes into Teams without requiring employees and agents to adopt an entirely new service management system.


## **How a Teams Integration Fits a Portal-Based ITSM Model**


A Microsoft Teams integration can reduce some context switching, but it does not necessarily make Teams the complete service management environment.


### **Employee Intake Can Span Multiple Channels**


Internal service desks often receive requests through portals, email, Teams, Slack, and direct conversations.


Freshservice provides a structured system for managing those requests, while its Teams integration brings selected interactions into Microsoft Teams. Organizations can therefore keep established ITSM processes while giving users and agents another way to interact with them.


For teams evaluating the experience, the key question is where employees should start a request. Some organizations deliberately prefer structured service catalogs and forms. Others want the employee's conversation itself to become the service request.


### **Service Management Extends Beyond Chat**


Teams can make notifications and approvals more accessible, but broader administration, reporting, configuration, asset management, and ITSM processes are still part of the Freshservice environment.


That approach can suit organizations with mature IT service management requirements and established Freshservice processes.


Teams that instead want employee conversations to serve as the primary intake and resolution interface may prefer a conversational internal help desk model.


## **The Case for Conversational Internal Support**


Traditional service management starts with the ticket. Conversational service management can start with the employee's message.


For example, an employee might ask for access to a new application directly in an IT help channel. A conversational internal help desk can turn that request into a structured ticket, route it to the right team, apply an SLA, and preserve the conversation as part of the request history.


With[employee support](https://unthread.io/solutions/employee-support/?ref=unthread.io) , teams can keep internal requests closer to the communication channels employees already use.


That model can support workflows such as:


- **Onboarding and offboarding:** Coordinate access, equipment, documentation, and tasks across internal teams.
- **Access requests:** Route software and system access requests to the right owners.
- **Expense and procurement approvals:** Turn employee requests into structured approval workflows.
- **Private HR requests:** Handle payroll, parental leave, benefits, employee documents, and policy questions through private workflows.
- **Workplace operations:** Track equipment, facilities, and other employee service requests.


The advantage is not simply that chat is available. It is that the conversation itself becomes part of the structured service workflow.

## **What to Evaluate in a Microsoft Teams Internal Help Desk**


Choosing an internal help desk for Microsoft Teams involves more than checking whether a platform offers a Teams integration. Internal support leaders should evaluate how deeply Teams fits into the request lifecycle, from employee intake and routing to approvals, resolution, reporting, and follow-up.


### **Employee Request Experience**


Start by looking at how employees actually submit requests. A Teams integration may provide notifications and selected ticket actions while still relying on a separate service portal for structured intake. A conversational approach allows employees to start requests directly from the collaboration environment they already use.


For organizations trying to increase adoption of an[internal service desk](https://unthread.io/solutions/it-service-desk/?ref=unthread.io) , reducing unnecessary context switching can make the request process more natural. IT, HR, Finance, Procurement, and workplace teams should consider whether employees can submit common requests without having to find the correct portal, form, or service catalog entry first.


### **Routing and Workflow Automation**


Internal requests often require more than creating a ticket. Access requests may need manager approval, onboarding may involve several departments, and procurement requests may need Finance or security review.


Teams should therefore evaluate whether the platform can automatically:


- Identify the type of request
- Route it to the correct internal team
- Apply the appropriate priority or SLA
- Trigger approval workflows
- Escalate unresolved requests
- Update connected business systems
- Keep employees informed as the request progresses


With[workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations/?ref=unthread.io) , internal service teams can build processes around recurring requests rather than manually triaging each conversation.


### **AI Across Internal Service Workflows**


AI capabilities should also be evaluated in the context of the requests employees actually make. Answering common knowledge questions is useful, but internal service delivery can also require classification, routing, approvals, workflow execution, and escalation.


A[purpose-built AI agent](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai/?ref=unthread.io) can support repetitive workflows across IT, HR, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and workplace operations while handing more complex requests to the appropriate person.


### **Privacy and Sensitive Requests**


Not every internal request should appear in a shared Teams channel. HR questions, payroll concerns, employee documents, access issues, and some Finance or Legal requests may require private handling.


Organizations should check whether their internal help desk can preserve conversational intake while moving sensitive requests into appropriate private workflows. The goal is to give employees a convenient way to ask for help without compromising the controls internal teams need for confidential information.


### **Administration and Ongoing Changes**


Finally, teams should consider what happens after implementation. Routing rules, approval processes, departments, and service workflows change over time.


An effective internal help desk should let administrators adjust automations and request flows without rebuilding the employee experience. This is particularly important for organizations expanding[employee support](https://unthread.io/solutions/employee-support/?ref=unthread.io) beyond IT into HR, Finance, Procurement, and other shared services.

Freshservice may fit organizations that already rely on its broader ITSM environment and want Microsoft Teams to complement existing ticketing, service catalog, asset, and change management processes.


Unthread is particularly relevant when the goal is to make Slack or Microsoft Teams a primary starting point for internal requests and automate more of the workflow around those conversations.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What does the Freshservice Microsoft Teams integration do?**


Freshservice uses Microsoft Teams to extend parts of its service management workflow into the collaboration environment. Teams can be used for service desk interactions such as notifications, approvals, and request-related actions while Freshservice remains the underlying ITSM platform.


### **Is Freshservice suitable for internal support?**


Yes. Freshservice can support internal IT and employee service workflows through ticketing, service catalogs, asset management, approvals, and other ITSM capabilities. It can be particularly relevant for organizations already using structured ITSM processes.


### **Does Unthread work with Microsoft Teams or only Slack?**


Unthread supports internal service workflows across Microsoft Teams and Slack, along with additional intake channels such as email and portals. Its core model turns employee conversations and requests into structured tickets that can be routed, automated, tracked, and resolved.


### **Can Unthread handle private HR requests?**


Yes. Internal teams can use private workflows for sensitive requests such as payroll, parental leave, benefits, policy questions, and employee documents while maintaining structured ticket tracking.


### **What internal requests can Unthread automate?**


Unthread can support workflows across IT, HR, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and workplace operations. Its automation capabilities include routing, escalations, approvals, connected-system actions, knowledge-based responses, and other repetitive internal service workflows.
